title: GTA Market Update October 2026: Prices Dip, Buyers Have the Edge
description: TRREB's October 2026 numbers: GTA sales down 7.9%, benchmark price down 4.3%. What it means for Brampton buyers and sellers, and how to use it.
hero_sub: TRREB's October numbers are in. Prices are lower than a year ago, buyers can negotiate, and the month-over-month trend is starting to firm up.

stats.label: GTA home sales in October (down 7.9% y/y)
MLS HPI Composite benchmark, year over year

takeaways: GTA home sales fell 7.9% and the benchmark price fell 4.3% compared to October 2025 (TRREB).
Seasonally adjusted, sales and prices edged up from September, so the market may be finding its footing.
Higher borrowing costs have been partly offset by lower prices, according to TRREB.
Buyers still have room to negotiate; sellers win with accurate pricing and strong presentation.

sections.label: THE SHORT ANSWER
sections.h2: What happened in the GTA housing market in October 2026?
sections.html:
The Toronto Regional Real Estate Board (TRREB) reported 5,603 home sales through its MLS® System in October 2026, down 7.9% from October 2025. New listings came in at 14,173, down 11.9%.

Prices were lower too. The MLS® Home Price Index (HPI) Composite benchmark was down 4.3% year over year, and the average selling price was $1,024,108, down 2.7%.

TRREB said uncertainty around inflation, borrowing costs and the economy kept many GTA buyers on the sidelines.

sections.label: THE TREND
sections.html:
Compared with last year, the numbers are down. But on a seasonally adjusted basis, TRREB reported that sales and new listings were up from September 2026, and both the benchmark and average price edged up month over month.

One month does not make a trend, but it is worth watching. Buyers who wait for a clear bottom often find that competition has already returned by the time it is obvious.

Affordability check: TRREB noted that while monthly mortgage payments on an average-priced home have edged up from a year ago, they are still much more affordable than in 2023 and 2024, because lower prices have helped offset higher borrowing costs.

sections.label: FOR BUYERS
sections.h2: What this means if you're buying in Brampton or the GTA
sections.html:
Buyers have negotiating power right now. In Brampton neighbourhoods popular with first-time buyers, such as Sandringham-Wellington, Northgate, Bram East and Vales of Castlemore, that can mean room on price, conditions or closing dates.

  1. Get pre-approved first. Know your real budget and rate hold before you shop.
  2. Look at what homes actually sold for, not asking prices, on the streets you like.
  3. Keep your conditions. In a slower market, financing and inspection conditions are more often accepted.
  4. Budget for closing costs on top of your down payment: land transfer tax, legal fees, inspection and adjustments.

First-time buyer? The FHSA and RRSP Home Buyers' Plan can help with your down payment if you qualify. See how to stack the FHSA and HBP.

sections.label: FOR SELLERS
sections.h2: What this means if you're selling
sections.html:
With fewer new listings than last year, well-prepared homes still stand out. What matters most in this market:

#1

Price it right from day one

Overpriced homes sit, and longer days on market usually lead to a lower final price.

#2

Presentation

Clean, staged, well-photographed homes get more showings and stronger offers.

#3

Know your local comps

GTA-wide averages hide big differences between neighbourhoods and home types.

faq.q: Are GTA home prices going down in 2026?
faq.a: Compared with a year earlier, yes. TRREB reported the October 2026 MLS HPI Composite benchmark was down 4.3% and the average selling price was down 2.7% compared to October 2025. Seasonally adjusted, both edged up from September 2026.

faq.q: How many homes sold in the GTA in October 2026?
faq.a: TRREB reported 5,603 home sales through its MLS System in October 2026, down 7.9% from October 2025.

faq.q: What was the average home price in the GTA in October 2026?
faq.a: The average selling price was $1,024,108, down 2.7% year over year, according to TRREB.

faq.q: Is it a good time to buy a home in Brampton?
faq.a: Buyers currently have more negotiating power than in recent years, but the right time depends on your finances, job security and plans. Get pre-approved, compare recent sold prices and speak with a local agent before deciding.

faq.q: Should I wait to sell my home?
faq.a: It depends on your next move and timeline. If you are buying and selling in the same market, lower prices can work in your favour on the purchase. A local price analysis will show what your home could sell for today.
